question.text: A small-cap equity fund would most likely be placed at which level of the Risk-o-meter?

explanation.text: The Logic: Small-cap equity funds invest in shares of small companies, which are typically more volatile, less liquid, and more sensitive to economic shocks than mid- and large-cap stocks. Because the underlying portfolio sits at the high end of equity-market volatility, these schemes are typically placed at the "Very High" level on the SEBI Risk-o-meter — the highest rung on the six-level scale. The Trap: "Low" and "Low to Moderate" describe overnight, liquid, and short-duration debt schemes — not small-cap equity. "Moderate" fits balanced or conservative hybrid schemes. None of these capture the volatility profile of a small-cap equity portfolio. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (37-39, 76, 79, 104, 110) support small-cap fund classification and general mutual fund risks but do not explicitly map a small-cap equity fund to the "Very High" Risk-o-meter rung. The framing above reflects general industry practice and SEBI's risk-classification scheme.
